# Weld

- Inherits [`Instance`](instance.md)
- Created with `Instance.new("Weld")`

Holds one part at a fixed offset from another. `Part1` is no longer simulated on its own; every tick it is moved to follow `Part0`. Use it to attach something to a character or to another moving part.

A weld does not make the physics solver treat the two parts as one object; use a `FixedConstraint` for that. A weld is refused if its two parts are already connected by other welds, directly or through a chain.

This page lists the members this class declares. Inherited members are
listed on the page of the class that declares them.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `C0` | `CFrame` | — | read/write | The offset of the weld on `Part0`. The weld keeps `Part0.CFrame * C0` equal to `Part1.CFrame * C1`. |
| `C1` | `CFrame` | — | read/write | The offset of the weld on `Part1`. The weld keeps `Part0.CFrame * C0` equal to `Part1.CFrame * C1`. |
| `Enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | read/write | Whether the weld holds. Disabling it returns `Part1` to the simulation where it is, with no velocity. |
| `Part0` | `Instance?` | — | read/write | The part or attachment that `Part1` follows. It can be simulated, anchored or a `CharacterBody`. Use a `Bone` here to attach an object to a joint of an animated character, such as a sword to a hand. Only a `BasePart` or an `Attachment` is accepted. |
| `Part1` | `BasePart?` | — | read/write | The part that follows `Part0`. While the weld is enabled, only the weld moves it: gravity does not affect it, and a `CFrame` you set is overwritten at the next tick. It must be a part, not an attachment. |
